topics.title: Devising from a text extract and a practitioner

outcomes.text: Explore one key extract in the context of the whole text, deconstructing its themes, structure, characters and style.
Apply one practitioner's methods, style and conventions to the devised piece.
Research themes and contexts, choose style and genre, and shape pace, tempo, scene order and audience impact.
Develop ideas in an ensemble through workshops, rehearsal, research and watching live theatre.
Use vocal expression, physicality, proxemics and audience engagement, refining work towards artistic intentions.
Develop a design concept for costume, lighting, set or sound and make design choices for an audience.
Analyse and evaluate ideas, research, decisions, collaboration, the final performance and realisation of intentions using subject terminology.
Read and research two extracts from different texts, placing each in its social, historical and cultural context.
Explain how style, structure, language, stage directions, character, space, audience relationship and design convey meaning.
Interpret text in rehearsal and performance as a performer or designer, working independently and collaboratively.
Analyse and evaluate a live performance as an informed audience member, using notes.
Explain how directors, performers and designers use space, audience relationships, voice and movement to communicate meaning.
Judge live theatre, analyse how performance and production elements combine, and use subject terminology.

topics.title: Page to stage: realising a performance text

outcomes.text: Study one List A text: Accidental Death of an Anarchist, Colder Than Here, Equus, Fences, Machinal or That Face.
Explore characterisation, staging, levels, proxemics, stage space, entrances and exits, mood, style and the playwright's structure.

subtopics.title: Realising an extract as performer and designer

outcomes.text: Propose how an unseen extract could be staged using voice, movement and design elements, and their intended audience impact.

topics.title: Interpreting a performance text for today

outcomes.text: Study one List B text: Antigone, Doctor Faustus, Hedda Gabler, Lysistrata, The Maids, The School for Scandal, The Tempest, Waiting for Godot or Woyzeck.
Act as director to outline and justify a production concept for a contemporary audience, considering venue, staging, design and acting style.
Explain how Artaud, Brecht, Berkoff, Complicite, Kneehigh, Littlewood, Punchdrunk or Stanislavski would shape the concept.
Research the original performance conditions and the social, historical and cultural context of the text.
Explain a practitioner's context, ideas, methods, artistic intentions, style, collaborations and audience relationship.
